Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event
My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it

Negative Appraisals.value: People are not what they seem
The world is a dangerous place

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'My memories of the event come in disconnected pieces that do not fit together' directly conflicts with 'I can talk about what happened very easily.' For a severe mugging-related PTSD profile, markedly fragmented recall and very easy verbal access to the trauma narrative are hard to reconcile as describing the same current memory presentation.

issues.item: Memory: Verbal Access: I can talk about what happened very easily.
issues.explanation: The Memory node is internally incoherent for a severe mugging/robbery PTSD presentation: 'I can talk about what happened very easily' suggests low avoidance and relatively integrated, verbally accessible trauma memory, whereas simultaneously endorsing very vivid detailed recall and body-based painful reliving implies a highly sensory, distressing, poorly integrated trauma memory. This combination is possible in milder cases, but here it is hard to reconcile clinically within the same Memory profile. The Negative Appraisals items are coherent for robbery trauma, but the Memory selections do not fit cleanly with that node pattern or with the strong Negative Appraisals ↔ Memory linkage in the formulation.

issues.item: Constant Vigilance: I have to be especially careful because you never know what can happen next
issues.explanation: This item is more characteristic of ongoing threat/safety behavior than of a pure negative appraisal. In this profile, Threat is not endorsed and all Threat-related edges are inactive, while the active formulation is specifically centered on a Memory ↔ Negative Appraisals loop. The mistrust items fit robbery-related appraisals, but 'Constant Vigilance' introduces a prominent current-threat theme that is not supported elsewhere in the profile.

vignette:
Arjun was a 32-year-old man, married and working as a housekeeper in a busy hotel in downtown Chicago. For the most part, he had navigated life with a sense of optimism, despite the challenges that came with being a South Asian immigrant. However, everything shifted dramatically one late evening when he was walking home after a long shift. The streets were dimly lit, and he had been replaying the day's events in his mind, unaware of the shadow that lurked behind him. Out of nowhere, he was approached by two men who demanded his wallet. In a blink, the situation escalated; one of the men brandished a knife, and fear coursed through Arjun's body like a cold wave. He felt the sharpness of the blade against his skin, the adrenaline surging as he complied, handing over his belongings. They fled, leaving him shaken and alone. 

In the days that followed, Arjun found himself haunted by vivid memories of that night. The details were agonizingly clear: the glint of the knife, the rush of panic, and the way his heart raced as he felt the cold air around him. Each recollection brought with it a wave of physical pain that radiated through his body, as if he were reliving the experience in real-time. Sometimes, while washing linens in the hotel laundry, the sensations would hit him abruptly; he would feel the tightening in his chest, the clammy sweat, and the ache in his legs as he recalled the moment he had been forced to the ground. He would often pause, struggling to breathe, knowing what had happened but unable to articulate it to anyone, even himself. Words escaped him, leaving him feeling trapped in a silence that only deepened his agony.

As weeks turned into months, Arjun's perception of the world began to shift. He had come to believe that people weren't what they seemed; the friendly smiles of guests passing by felt disingenuous, masks hiding malicious intent. His mistrust seeped into every interaction, souring relationships with friends and family. He avoided public spaces, convinced that danger lurked around every corner, waiting for the moment he would let his guard down. This pervasive sense of danger transformed his world into a battleground, where he was constantly on alert. He found himself avoiding the streets he once walked with ease, opting for longer, less direct routes to get home, even if it meant arriving later than necessary. His colleagues began to notice his withdrawn demeanor, and Arjun felt the widening gap between himself and those around him. 

At home, the strain was palpable. His wife, Meera, struggled to understand the changes in him. Once a source of comfort, their conversations became fraught with tension. Arjun was short with her, unable to share the turmoil inside. "You don't get it," he would say, frustration spilling over. She would reach out, trying to connect, but his walls were impenetrable. He had convinced himself that opening up would only reveal his vulnerabilities, and that left him feeling even more exposed. Every time she mentioned a night out, his heart would race, and he would decline, finding excuses that rang increasingly hollow. He longed to enjoy life again, yet the thought of being in crowded spaces or unfamiliar places made him feel trapped in a prison of his own making.

As time wore on, Arjun felt a growing sense of despair. It was a bleak realization that the fear he carried had seeped into every aspect of his life, overshadowing the joy he once felt in simple moments. He knew he needed help, but the thought of sharing his experience was terrifying. What frightened him most was the fear of being judged or misunderstood, of revealing the deep scars that the mugging had left on his psyche. Yet, amidst the turmoil, a small flicker of hope remained; he wanted to reclaim his life, to feel safe and whole again. It was this flicker that finally prompted him to seek help, driven by the desire to rebuild the trust he had lost in himself and in the world around him. Arjun sat in the waiting room of the therapist's office, heart racing, wondering if he would find the words he had longed to say for so many months - words that might help him unravel the pain and fear that had taken up residence in his life.
